title: Annotatio VI §.V open: Classis III Rationativa — spiritual food; Indigni not orally
pass_a_gloss: §. V. There follows the THIRD CLASS of Arguments, Rational indeed, but sacred — i.e. consisting by a middle term of Revelation — by which it is inferred (1) from the spiritual Nature of the thing to be eaten, that the unworthy eat Christ’s body in no mode, and so neither orally, because namely Christ’s body, food merely Spiritual, is Supernatural, and therefore to be taken in a merely Spiritual and Supernatural mode.
pass_b_english: §.V opens the third class: rational, but sacred — middle term from revelation.
(1) From the nature of the spiritual food: the unworthy eat Christ’s body in no mode, Oral included — it is merely spiritual and supernatural food, to be taken only that way.
source_text: §. V. Succedit TERTIA Argumentorum CLASSIS, Rationativa quidem, sed sacra, i. e. mediò Revelationis terminô constans, quô infertur (1) ex Natura rei manducandæ spirituali, indignos nullô, eóque nec orali modo, corpus Christi manducare, quia nempe corpus Christi, cibus merè Spiritualis, est Supernaturalis, indeque modo merè Spirituali & Supernaturali sumendus.
